title: Adaptive prompt fission architecture scratchpad
content:
Context / why I'm thinking about this:
- We get a lot of requests where a single user prompt contains several distinct sub-tasks (e.g., summarize + extract entities + rewrite). Currently we either run a monolithic prompt on one model (costly) or run sequential calls (adds latency).
- Idea: "prompt fission" — split a single input into per-subtask fragments, route each fragment to the optimal model/pipeline, then stitch results back at the proxy. Aim: lower cost while keeping SLOs for tail latency and coherence.

Goals (informal):
- Minimize total token cost compared to naive single-model generation
- Keep 95th percentile latency within 1.6x of a single-model call for 90% of traffic
- Ensure deterministic/traceable provenance for stitched outputs
- Keep API simple for product teams (single call, optional hints)

High-level architecture (sketch):

Client
  |
  v
Fission Proxy (stateless) --- config / policy -> Routing Engine
  |                            |
  |                            v
  |                       Cost & SLO model (history)
  v
Splitter (extracts subtasks + metadata)
  |
  v
Router -> parallel calls to Model Pools (summarizer, extractor, rewrite, cheap tokenizer-only models)
  |
  v
Merger (apply merge rules, normalization, ranking, conflict resolution)
  |
  v
Response (with provenance + cost report)

Notes about pieces:
- Splitter: combination of heuristic + tiny classification model. Output: list of fragments {id, role, start_tok, end_tok, hint}.
- Router: policy layer that uses fragment.role, size, user_tier, and recent SLOs to pick pool (e.g., redwood-small-quant, community-flan, private-dedicated-gpu).
- Merger: deterministic glue logic + optional rerank step. For some use cases we should run a small consistency pass that can mutate outputs to ensure ordering/coherence.

API shape (draft) — aim for one request, optional per-fragment overrides:
POST /v1/prompt-fission/generate\Headers: Authorization, X-User-Tier\Body:
{
  "input": "<raw user text>",
  "hints": ["prefer-cheap-for-extraction"],
  "fission_config": {
    "max_fragments": 5,
    "fragment_strategy": "semantic-split", // semantic | fixed-window | explicit-markers
    "merge_policy": "strict-provenance" // strict-provenance | best-effort | rerank
  },
  "client_trace_id": "...",
  "timeout_ms": 3000
}

Response (sketch):
{
  "output": "<stitched result>",
  "fragments": [
    {"id":"f1","role":"summarize","model":"flan-small","latency_ms":47,"tokens":34},
    {"id":"f2","role":"extract_entities","model":"cheap-ner","latency_ms":28,"tokens":12}
  ],
  "cost_estimate": {"tokens": 123, "approx_usd": "0.0009"},
  "provenance": "sha256:...",
  "warnings": ["fragment f2 truncated due to token cap"]
}

Config sketch (proxy-level YAML) — policies that ops teams can tune:
---
fission_policies:
  default:
    fragment_strategy: semantic-split
    max_fragments: 4
    latency_budget_ms: 250
    cost_target_usd_per_1k: 0.50
  enterprise_tier:
    max_fragments: 6
    latency_budget_ms: 500
    preferred_pools: [private-dedicated-gpu]
routing:
  pools:
    - name: cheap-ner
      capabilities: [ner, extract]
      qps_limit: 200
      cost_score: 0.2
    - name: flan-small
      capabilities: [summarize, rewrite]
      qps_limit: 400
      cost_score: 0.6
    - name: longform-gptish
      capabilities: [summarize, creative]
      qps_limit: 50
      cost_score: 1.2

Cost & SLO model (notes):
- Each routing decision emits a "cost score" and expected latency distribution conditioned on fragment size. We maintain EWMA per-pool latency and tail multipliers to bias routing when SLO is threatened.
- When predicted end-to-end > latency_budget_ms, prefer fewer fragments and more powerful pools (fallback to single composite call).
- Track per-client rolling window of cost to enforce soft budget hints.

Merge strategies (brainstorm):
- strict-provenance: attach each fragment output with source, order by original span. No hallucinated bridging text allowed; if gaps, append TODO markers.
- best-effort: merger can synthesize bridging sentences using a small model; risk of subtle hallucination but better UX.
- rerank-then-merge: generate n candidates per fragment and run a consistency pass that optimizes coherence score.

Edge cases / open questions:
- How to handle fragments that need cross-fragment context (e.g., anaphora)? Options: include prefix context windows, or run a final light-weight coherence pass that has access to fragment outputs plus original text.
- Billing: do we surface per-fragment costs to external customers? privacy/legal concerns if mapping cost to model pools (enterprise might care).
- Consistency vs cost: for legal/regulatory use-cases we might require strict-provenance always; need per-customer policy enforcement.
- State explosion: if fragments are retriable, we must keep idempotency keys and fragment-level checkpoints.

Quick notes-to-self on experiments to run:
- Baseline: run whole prompt on flan-small vs fission split (semantic) -> measure median cost, p50/p95 latency, and manual coherence eval on 100 samples.
- Ablation: include prefix-window of 128 tokens vs none for cross-fragment refs.
- Routing policy: AW-Bandit style that trades cost and latency; simulate with synthetic traffic.

Next actions:
- Draft proto -> small internal PR that implements splitter + router skeleton (Ethan)
- Build lightweight merger in Python for eval harness (Priya)
- Prepare UX API that product teams can opt into (Liang)

Notes / stray ideas:
- "tenant-aware fission": for heavy enterprise, allow them to upload custom merge templates so final text adheres to style/legal tokens.
- Telemetry: emit fragment-level traces, and an aggregated "fission-score" per request (cost saving, latency multiplier, coherence_penalty).

References / links:
- Related ticket: JIRA:ENG-1342 (proto routing policy)
- Internal mockup repo: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-fission-proto/pull/47
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime "prompt-fission initial" (link pinned in PR)

Random TODOs:
- [ ] Add deterministic hashing for provenance that encodes model+weights+merge-policy
- [ ] Add an opt-out header for customers who require single-model canonical outputs
- [ ] Write a short product one-pager that explains tradeoffs for PMs

End of scratchpad.
